claims.text: As-fabricated additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components may contain fabrication-induced defects.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components relative to untreated components.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components relative to untreated components.
Deep cryogenic treatment reduces fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Nonequilibrium chemical short-range order mediates the effects of deep cryogenic treatment.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces a phase transition in additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases lattice distortion in additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
The DCT-induced phase transition and lattice distortion cause improved mechanical integrity.
The DCT-induced phase transition and lattice distortion cause improved dimensional precision.
The DCT-induced phase transition and lattice distortion cause a reduction in fabrication-induced defects.
The relevant baseline is an as-fabricated additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy component without DCT.
The effects of DCT on high-entropy-alloy properties are not yet fully understood.
Chemical short-range order may be useful for tailoring high-entropy-alloy properties.
A controlled comparison of otherwise equivalent additively manufactured components with and without DCT can test the hypothesis.
Failure of DCT-treated components to improve dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and defect reduction relative to untreated controls would falsify the hypothesis.
